answer: Sybil attacks can be mitigated by requiring agents to solve verifiable delay functions before each consensus horizon. Nodes must complete sequential cryptographic proofs to retain execution slots, preventing a dune of synthetic workers from overwhelming task queues. An attacker incurs non-parallelizable CPU time and energy costs per identity, even when masked by sable proxies. However, this imposes latency overhead on time-critical agents and remains vulnerable to specialized ASIC hardware.
